subject.title: doctor --fix migrates codex/gpt-5.5 to openai/gpt-5.5, then Codex app-server startup times out on 2026.6.1

question: Should unsafe legacy Codex routes be retained with manual-migration warnings until doctor can prove the migrated OpenAI/Codex app-server route is healthy, or should doctor continue unconditional canonicalization and handle startup failures separately?
rationale: Current main still applies the migration and open PRs split the solution between doctor migration policy and Codex startup lifecycle proof; choosing the permanent upgrade contract is maintainer product direction.

options.title: Accept plan-gated doctor migration
options.body: Treat https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/93180 as the canonical migration-policy path and keep this issue open for merged proof plus any startup-side follow-up.

options.title: Require startup proof first
options.body: Hold the migration-policy decision until https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/89442 or live reporter-account proof establishes the app-server timeout boundary.

options.title: Keep unconditional canonicalization
options.body: Reject retained legacy routes and require a separate Codex app-server availability fix before closing this issue.

recommendation.title: Accept plan-gated doctor migration
recommendation.body: Treat https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/93180 as the canonical migration-policy path and keep this issue open for merged proof plus any startup-side follow-up.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete is the strongest history signal for OpenAI provider identity unification and the current doctor migration policy surface.
